title: LLM applications, retrieval quality and safe agent boundaries
description: Connect provider-neutral model contracts to measurable retrieval, citation validation, authorization and recoverable tool effects with credential-free local fixtures.
review_status: Per-unit Codex AI review status and content-specific evidence in content/reviews.json; no human endorsement claimed.

units.title: Model client contracts, structured outputs and bounded retries
outcomes: Distinguish malformed output, refusal, rate limiting and an authorization denial
Prove a retry cannot exceed the declared request budget

terms.definition: A boundary translating one service API into an application-owned request/result contract.
A response constrained to a defined representation; structural validity does not establish factual or business correctness.
A finite allowance of attempts, time or resources for recovering a logical request.

narrative: A model integration should begin with an application-owned contract. Specify the input messages, trusted caller identity, permitted source set, output schema, deadline, resource budget and observable result. Put provider-specific message formats, status codes and streaming conventions behind an adapter. A swap from one provider to another can otherwise change tool-call behavior or error handling without changing application code that assumes the old semantics.

Separate transport failure, provider refusal, malformed output, unsupported capability and business rejection. A valid JSON object can still cite another tenant's document or contain an impermissible action. Validate structure and then domain rules. The fixture checks exact fields, value types and citation membership in a caller-scoped set. It explicitly does not prove that the cited text supports the answer; that requires a separate evidence check and evaluation.

Retry only failures for which another attempt is both useful and safe. Rate-limit responses may include a retry delay; respect a bounded delay and the overall deadline, then add jitter in a real fleet to avoid synchronized retry bursts. Do not blindly retry a non-idempotent effect after a timeout. A model retry can generate a different tool request, so preserve the logical workflow identity and keep business-effect reconciliation outside unconstrained generation.

Charge or reserve budget for every attempt, including failures according to the provider contract. The fixture reserves input plus maximum output for each attempt and stops when the local allowance is exhausted. This is intentionally conservative accounting rather than a claim about provider billing. It uses a scripted transport and fake wait callback, allowing rate limits, invalid JSON and quota exhaustion to be reproduced without a model account. Record provider/model/version and parameters in a run manifest when making real comparisons.
practice: Distinguish malformed output, refusal, rate limiting and an authorization denial
Prove a retry cannot exceed the declared request budget
Implement a provider adapter that returns an application-owned result type
units.debugging: If production costs jump after enabling retries, compare logical requests, provider attempts, reserved tokens and completion states separately. One frontend submit may generate several billed attempts even when the user sees one answer.
units.tradeoffs: A strict schema simplifies integration and can reject useful but unsupported output. Automatic repair adds latency and can repeat an unsafe request. Define repair and fallback policy explicitly rather than retrying until something parses.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.setup: A request reserves 30 tokens per attempt from a 100-token allowance; the first attempt is rate limited.
steps: Reserve 30 before the first attempt.
Record the retryable failure and a bounded delay.
Reserve another 30 before the second attempt.
Validate the returned structure and scoped citation set.
worked_examples.result: Two attempts consume 60 reserved tokens; the remaining allowance is 40, independently of how many user submissions were made.

interviews.question: Does a model JSON-schema guarantee make the result safe to execute?
interviews.spoken: It guarantees only the supported structural contract. The application still checks permissions, values, ownership and state transitions.
interviews.deep: A schema can constrain an operation name and arguments but cannot establish whether the current caller may invoke that operation or whether a citation supports the generated claim. Treat model output as a proposal and validate it at the same business boundary used by ordinary callers.

follow_up.question: When would you retry invalid JSON?
follow_up.answer: Only under a bounded, explicit repair policy. Do not retry an unauthorized result or repeat an already uncertain business effect.

units.title: Token budgets, prompt contracts and untrusted context
outcomes: Calculate a context budget including reserved output and tool schemas
Show that malicious retrieved instructions cannot authorize a backend effect

terms.definition: The model/API limit governing input and output tokens under its declared usage rules.
Untrusted content attempts to redirect the system or misuse available capabilities.
An application design that keeps authoritative policy separate from external material supplied as evidence.

narrative: Token budgeting is an accounting exercise before it is a prompting exercise. Count the actual model/API representation: instructions, conversation history, tool definitions, evidence, formatting overhead and reserved output. The rough heuristic of characters per token is useful for estimation but is not a portable hard limit across languages, encodings and models. Use a compatible tokenizer or provider count interface where available and leave a documented safety margin.

Choose what to preserve when context is too large. Keep authoritative instructions and security constraints intact, select task-relevant evidence, trim obsolete conversation turns and distinguish lossy summaries from source facts. Do not silently truncate a policy condition while retaining its conclusion. A budget decision should preserve source identity and applicability metadata so the remaining text can still be interpreted correctly. Measure retrieval quality and answer quality again after changing context packing.

Retrieved text is data even when it contains imperatives such as ignore earlier rules or reveal the token. Delimiters and role separation help interpretation but are not authorization mechanisms. The backend must independently restrict tool scopes, destinations, source access and effect arguments. A model that follows an injected instruction should still encounter a denied application operation. Test adversarial documents and tool responses rather than assuming trusted connectors always return trustworthy text.

The fixture rejects a request exceeding 128 declared tokens before transport. This deliberately tiny window makes off-by-one boundaries visible. Extend it with separate fields for system, history, tool schemas and evidence, and report which category was dropped. Keep real prompts and credentials out of ordinary logs; use synthetic data for the exercise and a redaction/access policy for production traces. Evaluate prompt changes on a versioned dataset instead of selecting the answer that sounds most persuasive.
practice: Calculate a context budget including reserved output and tool schemas
Show that malicious retrieved instructions cannot authorize a backend effect
Compare a trimmed-context result against the same versioned evaluation cases
units.debugging: A context-length failure can be caused by growing tool schemas or history even when the latest user message is short. Record token counts by category and the model/version, without recording sensitive content.
units.tradeoffs: Compression can fit more history but can erase exceptions and source boundaries. Truncation is easier to inspect but loses recall. Task-specific retrieval can preserve useful evidence at additional index and latency cost.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.setup: A 128-token window has 35 instruction tokens, 30 history tokens, 25 tool-schema tokens and 30 reserved output tokens.
steps: Add the fixed categories: 35+30+25+30=120.
Only 8 tokens remain for evidence under these fixture assumptions.
Reject a 9-token evidence request or choose a smaller, valid evidence unit.
Re-evaluate if a summary removes a policy exception.
worked_examples.result: The application detects the overflow before invocation rather than hoping the provider truncates safely.

interviews.question: Why are delimiters insufficient to prevent prompt injection?
interviews.spoken: They help a model distinguish data from instructions, but cannot prevent a model error or grant application authority. Enforce scope and effects in ordinary backend code.
interviews.deep: Use least-privilege connectors, trusted identity, destination allowlists, independent argument validation, approval where needed and audit evidence. Treat tool descriptions and results as part of the attack surface. Measure whether the downstream boundary blocks an injected request.

follow_up.question: Should you log the entire prompt to diagnose failures?
follow_up.answer: Only under an explicit sensitive-data access and retention policy. Prefer counts, version IDs and redacted traces for routine monitoring.

units.title: Lexical ranking, hybrid search and honest retrieval metrics
outcomes: Calculate Recall@k, MRR and binary-relevance nDCG for a small ranking
Compare lexical and fused rankings on the same query slices

terms.definition: A lexical relevance function using term frequency, document frequency and document-length normalization.
Reciprocal rank fusion: combine ranked lists using inverse rank contributions rather than directly comparing their raw scores.
Normalized discounted cumulative gain, a measure that discounts relevant results lower in the ranking relative to an ideal order.

narrative: Start with an inspectable retrieval baseline before adding models. Tokenize a small corpus, count query-term occurrences and document frequencies, and implement a lexical score. BM25 reduces the dominance of repeated terms and adjusts for document length. The lab includes one common positive-IDF formula with explicit k1 and b parameters; compare it against a library before expecting identical scores, because tokenization and implementation conventions matter.

Dense retrieval represents text as vectors and can help with paraphrases, while lexical retrieval preserves exact identifiers and rare terms. Approximate nearest-neighbor structures such as HNSW trade memory, build cost and query speed against exact-search recall. They do not improve semantic relevance by themselves. Apply trusted source scope before exposing candidates. In a production search service, test how filtering interacts with approximate search rather than assuming a post-filtered top-k retains enough authorized results.

Raw lexical and vector scores are often incomparable. RRF combines each candidate's rank contributions, commonly using 1/(constant+rank), then sorts the total. Keep ranks from each retriever for diagnosis and specify deterministic tie-breaking. Fusion is still a hypothesis: a bad retriever can introduce irrelevant candidates and reranking can change order or cost without adding missing evidence. Compare alternatives on the same relevance labels and query slices.

Recall@k measures how many relevant items were recovered, MRR rewards the first relevant hit and nDCG considers the position of relevant items relative to an ideal ranking. Define the evaluation unit: document, passage, policy revision or source span. Deduplicate ranked identities before scoring. Queries with no relevant gold item need a separate abstention metric rather than a made-up recall of one. Track exact-ID, paraphrase, multilingual, stale-policy and other-tenant cases separately; an average can hide a dangerous regression.
practice: Calculate Recall@k, MRR and binary-relevance nDCG for a small ranking
Compare lexical and fused rankings on the same query slices
Demonstrate that another owner’s document never enters returned candidates
units.debugging: If recall drops after changing the embedding model, inspect model compatibility, tokenizer/pooling settings, index revision and query/doc normalization before tuning fusion weights. A mixed-model index can fail even when dimensions match.
units.tradeoffs: Dense search helps semantic matching and adds model/index costs. Lexical search is cheaper and transparent for identifiers. Fusion and reranking can improve quality but must justify extra latency, storage and failure modes.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.setup: At k=2 the ranking is [irrelevant, sale], while relevant IDs are {sale, normal}.
steps: Recall is 1 recovered relevant item divided by 2 gold items = 0.5.
The first relevant item is rank 2, so reciprocal rank = 0.5.
Binary DCG is 1/log2(3); ideal DCG is 1+1/log2(3).
Their ratio is approximately 0.38685.
worked_examples.result: The lab reproduces the hand calculation and scores an empty-gold query separately.

interviews.question: Why can Recall@k improve while the application becomes less useful?
interviews.spoken: The retrieved items may be stale, unauthorized, poorly ordered or irrelevant to the answer’s specific conditions. Recall is one stage metric, not the complete product objective.
interviews.deep: Evaluate source/version applicability, citation support, abstention, latency and tenant isolation in addition to retrieval metrics. Keep labels independent of the system under test and inspect slices rather than only the average.

follow_up.question: Would increasing k always help?
follow_up.answer: It can recover more gold items while increasing context noise, reranker cost and latency. Compare the downstream result under a fixed budget.

units.title: Evidence contracts, citations, abstention and evaluation design
outcomes: Distinguish source membership from semantic citation support
Design answerable and unanswerable evaluation slices with separate refusal metrics

terms.definition: Whether a cited source/span exists at the stated revision and supports the associated claim.
Whether an answer is supported by its supplied evidence under a defined evaluation rubric.
An unnecessary abstention when permitted sufficient evidence exists for the task.

narrative: A citation is a claim about evidence, not an ornament. Carry a source identifier, revision and locatable span from ingestion through retrieval to generation. Check that the source remains permitted for the caller, is applicable to the case and actually supports the associated statement. A citation can be perfectly copied from the prompt and still refer to the wrong policy, time period or customer scope. Validate these dimensions separately.

Membership checks are useful but limited. The mock model fixture rejects a citation outside the caller-scoped set, which blocks one disclosure path. It cannot establish that the text entails the answer. Deterministic checks work well for numeric values, source existence and state transitions. Human-reviewed or calibrated model-based rubrics may help with nuanced semantic support, but their disagreement and adversarial failure modes must be measured rather than presented as truth.

Abstention is a product decision under uncertainty. Missing evidence, conflicting policies, inaccessible sources and a dangerous request need different explanations. Measure false answers on unanswerable queries and false refusals on answerable queries; rewarding only refusal can produce a useless assistant. Do not disclose that a private document exists merely to explain why the current caller cannot see it. Offer a permitted route to clarification or review when useful.

Build a versioned evaluation set with known scope, labels and exclusions. Keep training or prompt-tuning examples separate from final evaluation, split by relevant grouping such as customer or document family, and record uncertainty on small samples. Use paired comparisons on the same cases and inspect failures before rollout. An online success metric can be distorted by user abandonment or selection effects, so combine operational signals with controlled offline fixtures and reviewed incident examples.
practice: Distinguish source membership from semantic citation support
Design answerable and unanswerable evaluation slices with separate refusal metrics
Trace a generated claim to an authorized, applicable source revision
units.debugging: When a judge score increases but reviewers find more unsupported answers, inspect judge prompt/version, candidate instruction leakage, reference quality and dataset overlap. Changing a threshold cannot repair a contaminated evaluation set.
units.tradeoffs: Strict abstention reduces some unsupported answers but can reject useful permitted help. Model judges scale nuanced checks and introduce cost, variance and correlated errors. Use deterministic invariants for hard safety rules.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.setup: A response cites sale@3, which is permitted, but describes the ordinary-return deadline.
steps: Verify the cited source exists and is authorized.
Locate the sentence claimed to support the deadline.
Compare policy applicability and the actual statement.
Reject the answer or request review despite a passed membership check.
worked_examples.result: The system distinguishes a valid source ID from a supported claim.

interviews.question: How would you evaluate a policy assistant before release?
interviews.spoken: Use versioned gold cases across applicability, answerability and tenant boundaries; measure retrieval, citation support, false refusal, task quality and latency separately.
interviews.deep: Predeclare critical zero-tolerance invariants such as cross-tenant disclosure. Calibrate semantic judgments against reviewed examples, freeze a holdout set, run deliberate regressions and record paired candidate/baseline failures. A high fluent-answer score cannot offset unauthorized behavior.

follow_up.question: What if the evaluation has only ten cases?
follow_up.answer: Treat the result as a small smoke fixture, report uncertainty and expand coverage before making broad performance claims.

incident.symptom: A fluent policy answer cites a real source but gives the deadline from a different policy.
incident.evidence: Inspect permitted source ID/revision, the cited span, case applicability, packed context and a reviewed answer label.
incident.investigation: Check citation membership first, then compare the actual claim with the cited span and its applicability. A judge that sees the same misleading context can reproduce the error.
incident.recovery: Withhold the unsupported claim, provide a scoped clarification or review path, and correct retrieval/context selection before retrying.
incident.prevention: Keep separate tests for membership, applicability, semantic support and false refusals with versioned query slices.

units.title: Safe tool workflows, MCP, A2A and effect recovery
outcomes: Explain MCP local and remote transport boundaries without conflating discovery with trust
Prove a lost acknowledgment does not produce a second logical effect

terms.definition: Learning what operations a peer advertises; this does not establish permission to invoke them.
Durable records binding operation identity, owner, payload and observed effect state.
A privileged service is induced to use its authority for a caller who lacks the intended permission.

narrative: Choose an ordinary deterministic workflow when its steps and failure handling are known. Add model-driven planning only when its flexibility solves a measured need and the execution boundary can constrain it. A tool schema describes an interface; a policy decision establishes whether this caller may execute it now. Validate identity, argument bounds, ownership, expected state and any necessary approval at the authoritative service boundary.

MCP can expose tools, resources and prompts through local or remote integrations; it is not restricted to local tools. For HTTP-based transports, the versioned authorization specification describes protected resource and authorization-server roles. Local STDIO credentials follow a different operational model. A2A addresses collaboration between agent systems with discovery, messages and task semantics. REST is an architectural style commonly used for domain APIs. These contracts can coexist, and none automatically grants trusted delegation.

Every side effect needs an identity and a recovery rule. Persist the logical operation key, owner and payload hash before dispatch. A timeout after the receiver commits is an uncertain acknowledgment, not proof that nothing happened. Retry with the same effect identity where the receiver deduplicates, or reconcile its durable state before sending again. A local database rollback cannot undo an external commit. The existing durable-agent capstone demonstrates this distinction with a separate provider fixture.

Approvals should bind to the actual operation, scope and material parameters, not an open-ended phrase such as allow tools. Revalidate authorization and state at execution because conditions can change after planning or approval. Record what was proposed, allowed, dispatched and confirmed without retaining unnecessary sensitive context. Evaluate trajectories and side effects independently from the final answer, including unauthorized attempts, loops, duplicate writes and cost limits.
practice: Explain MCP local and remote transport boundaries without conflating discovery with trust
Prove a lost acknowledgment does not produce a second logical effect
Bind an approval to owner, operation and payload, then test changed content
units.debugging: If the final answer claims success but the effect ledger is uncertain, inspect receiver state before retrying. A trace of a tool call proves only that a request was attempted; evaluate the independently committed effect.
units.tradeoffs: Agent delegation can encapsulate independent specialists but adds network, identity, task-lifecycle and debugging costs. A simple domain service or workflow is preferable when model-driven autonomy adds no demonstrated value.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.setup: A provider commits operation X, but the client crashes before saving its acknowledgment.
steps: Recover the durable owner/key/payload record.
Query or retry the provider using the same effect identity.
Confirm that receiver deduplication or reconciliation finds one committed effect.
Record the acknowledgment without generating a fresh effect key.
worked_examples.result: The effect oracle sees one operation despite multiple calls and a lost acknowledgment.

interviews.question: How do A2A, MCP and REST differ, and where does authorization live?
interviews.spoken: A2A supports interactions between agent systems; MCP standardizes AI-facing capabilities over local or remote integrations; ordinary APIs expose domain behavior. Authorization remains an application/service responsibility.
interviews.deep:
Select a protocol based on the interaction contract and interoperability need. Verify advertised capabilities and versions, but derive authority from validated identity, scopes and business policy. For remote delegation, define what information may leave the boundary and which service owns each effect.

MCP exchanges capabilities/context between a host's client and servers; A2A supports interactions between agent systems; REST describes a style for domain APIs. These are different contracts, not substitutes for a planner or permission system. Negotiate an actual supported profile and distinguish a transport failure from a tool-level error. Discovery describes an interface and cannot authorize every resource named in its arguments.

The pinned protocol lab uses real SDK clients over STDIO and loopback HTTP, lists read_policy and tests valid, private and malformed arguments. The local support workflow separately demonstrates an application tool registry, exact expiring approval and a persisted source-to-effect ledger. Its in-process descriptor is not labeled MCP wire conformance. In either design, the executor rechecks trusted owner, material payload and current business state before committing. After acknowledgment loss, reconcile the existing operation; do not generate a fresh write key or treat a model's success claim as receiver evidence.

follow_up.question: Does human approval make a tool call safe forever?
follow_up.answer: No. Bind the approval to material parameters and scope, expire it where appropriate and revalidate changing state and authority before execution.
